tagline: A Mekong border town across from Savannakhet — the Indochina Market, Ho Kaeo Mukdahan tower, and the rock views of Phu Pha Thoep
introHtml: Mukdahan is a small town on the Mekong, sitting directly across from Savannakhet in Laos. The 2nd Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge crosses over easily, so people come here to enjoy the riverfront and pop across the border into Laos on the same trip. In town, the Ho Kaeo Mukdahan tower gives 360-degree views over the city and the river. The riverside Indochina Market sells goods from Laos and Vietnam alongside local souvenirs. Just out of town, Phu Pha Thoep National Park has clusters of oddly shaped rocks and wide-open views, while the temple on Phu Manorom looks down over the whole town and the curve of the Mekong. Mukdahan is also home to the Phu Thai people, who have their own culture and food. You can do the riverfront, the nature, or the border crossing — or all three.
bestTime: November–February is cool and comfortable — good for walking the riverfront, heading up the viewpoints, and visiting Phu Pha Thoep. Early in the rainy season the rocks at Phu Pha Thoep get a covering of moss and little wildflowers, which is pretty in its own way.

highlights.name: The riverfront and the bridge to Savannakhet
highlights.blurb: Mukdahan sits opposite Savannakhet in Laos, with the 2nd Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge crossing the Mekong. People like to take in the Thai-side riverfront and then cross over to walk the markets and town on the Lao side in one trip.

highlights.name: Ho Kaeo Mukdahan
highlights.blurb: A tall observation tower in the middle of town. Head up for views over the city, the Mekong, and the Lao side in every direction — it's the landmark and main viewpoint of Mukdahan.

highlights.name: Indochina Market
highlights.blurb: A riverside market in town selling clothes, household goods, and food from Laos and Vietnam mixed with local souvenirs. It's the main spot for shopping and gifts in the province.

highlights.name: Phu Pha Thoep National Park
highlights.blurb: A park with clusters of oddly shaped rocks scattered across a wide stone plateau. You can wander the rocks and stay for sunset — it's Mukdahan's best-known nature spot.

highlights.name: Wat Phu Manorom
highlights.blurb: A hilltop temple with a giant naga and a viewpoint, looking down over the town of Mukdahan and the curve of the Mekong. People come up to pay respects and take in the view.

highlights.name: Phu Thai culture
highlights.blurb: Mukdahan is home to the Phu Thai people, who have their own language, dress, and food. The Nong Sung district area especially still keeps the old ways and its weaving traditions alive.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, laap, koi, grilled chicken, and bold bamboo-shoot soup are everyday meals here, like across the rest of the region. You'll find them in every corner of town.

foodScene.name: Mekong river fish
foodScene.note: Riverside spots cook freshwater fish — grilled, in tom yum, as laap pla, and big pla khang catfish. Sit out for the cool breeze and the view across to Laos.

foodScene.name: Phu Thai food
foodScene.note: Local Phu Thai dishes like bamboo-shoot curry, pla daek bong, and sharp fermented foods. You'll find them around Nong Sung district and at local cultural events.

foodScene.name: Vietnamese food
foodScene.note: Nem nueang, mu yo, and fresh spring rolls turn up in town, thanks to the riverside communities and the back-and-forth across the border.

foodScene.name: Snacks at the Indochina Market
foodScene.note: The riverside market has snacks from Laos and Vietnam alongside local ones to graze on — grilled and fried bites and sweets. It's a favorite spot for street food.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and grilled meats
foodScene.note: Mu kratha (DIY hotpot-barbecue) places are all over town — the dinner where groups meet up, especially in the town center and near the riverfront road.

foodScene.name: Mekong-view cafes
foodScene.note: There are cafes and coffee shops opening onto the Mekong and the town. Stop for a coffee before heading out to the market or up to a viewpoint.

foodScene.name: Mu yo and naem to take home
foodScene.note: Mu yo, naem, and Isan sausage are the well-known gifts people take home. Pick them up at shops around town and at the Indochina Market.

attractions.name: Ho Kaeo Mukdahan
attractions.blurb: A tall observation tower in the middle of town. Head up for views over the city, the Mekong, and the Lao side in every direction — it's the landmark and main viewpoint of Mukdahan.

attractions.name: Indochina Market
attractions.blurb: A riverside market in town selling goods from Laos and Vietnam and local souvenirs — the place to shop and graze on street food by the water.

attractions.name: Phu Pha Thoep National Park
attractions.blurb: A wide stone plateau dotted with clusters of oddly shaped rocks. Wander the rocks and wait for sunset — it's the province's best-known nature spot.

attractions.name: Wat Phu Manorom
attractions.blurb: A hilltop temple with a giant naga and a viewpoint, looking down over the town of Mukdahan and the curve of the Mekong. People come up to pay respects and take photos.

attractions.name: 2nd Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
attractions.blurb: The bridge over the Mekong linking Mukdahan with Savannakhet in Laos. It's the main border crossing and the route on toward Vietnam via Laos.

attractions.name: Wat Roi Phra Phutthabat Phu Manorom
attractions.blurb: A temple on Phu Manorom with a Buddha footprint and a Buddha image to pay respects to, plus wide views of the town and the Mekong. A popular spot to make merit and take in the view.

attractions.name: Kaeng Kabao
attractions.blurb: A rocky stretch of the Mekong in Wan Yai district, where the water runs over a broad spread of boulders. Riverside restaurants let you sit with the cool breeze over a plate of river fish.

attractions.name: Nong Sung district, Phu Thai country
attractions.blurb: A Phu Thai community that still keeps its language, dress, weaving, and local food alive. Walk around to see the way of life and buy woven cloth to take home.
